title: Full-suite validation exposed a partial farmer lock and a tight dashboard health timeout
observation: A post-delivery full-suite run first found that two concurrent farmer once processes could enqueue the same failed turn. The lock creator makes the file visible with O_EXCL before writing its owner JSON; a contender that observed the brief incomplete file treated it as stale and unlinked it. A later full-suite run exposed DashboardService.health returning blocked after a timeout during its bounded status-projection request; this was observed under parallel suite load, and the status endpoint was the expensive second request in that code path.
impact: A concurrent farmer evaluation could duplicate one recovery queue action.
A slow but valid local dashboard status projection could produce a false blocked health report during load.
reusable_value: For cross-process file locks, an unreadable owner record immediately after exclusive create is an in-progress write until the existing stale-lock TTL expires. Keep local health requests bounded while allowing realistic status-projection latency; full-suite parallel load is useful evidence for both boundaries.
actions: acquireRecoveryLock now uses lock-file mtime when the owner JSON is incomplete and only reclaims that record after the existing TTL; a regression test preserves and then expires a partial lock.
DashboardService retains the health identity checks and raises the /api/status probe timeout from two to three seconds.
Retained every assertion; focused farmer tests pass 32/32 and the full suite passes 217/217 with architecture smoke 150 files and 12 variables.
